title: Why black influence goes unadmitted, Getz and Lester Young
summary: Sam and Ridley say egos and race keep players like Getz from crediting black influences.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: It's an interesting turnaround that's happening though. I've been noticing like some of the things that's been happening like with some of the newer white players that come on the scene, there is less of a reluctance to admit to any of the black influece. I mean there are certain exceptions. I mean to cut a guy like Niels, he's in another class. But there are some young, there is a young crop of dudes coming on the scene now, I notice that it's very
interesting what they th ought. Even Stan Getz won't even admit that Lester Young influenced him.
He'd be talking about Herbie Steward. He'd be talking about a whole bunch on knuckleheads, you know.
He won't admit it. I think it's part of that racial thing.
